## Goal

This notebook shows how to:

1. Read the **DIA-NN** example report shipped with
   [MSstatsConvert](https://github.com/Vitek-Lab/MSstatsConvert)
   (`inst/tinytest/raw_data/DIANN` on the `devel` branch)
2. Convert it to MSstats input with `DIANNtoMSstatsFormat()`
3. Summarise to **protein-level** intensities with `dataProcess()`
4. Reformat that protein table to **NPX-style** long data with
   OlinkAnalyze `MSstatstoNPX()`

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A[DIA-NN report + annotation] --> B[DIANNtoMSstatsFormat]
  B --> C[dataProcess ProteinLevelData]
  C --> D[MSstatstoNPX]
  D --> E[OlinkAnalyze NPX tibble]
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Dependencies

- **Bioconductor:** `MSstats`, `MSstatsConvert` (install with
  `BiocManager::install(c("MSstats", "MSstatsConvert"))`)
- **OlinkAnalyze:** this repo — load with `devtools::load_all("OlinkAnalyze")`
- Render from the **repository root**
:::

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
pkg_dir <- "OlinkAnalyze"
if (!dir.exists(pkg_dir)) {
  stop("Render / knit from the repo root (folder that contains OlinkAnalyze/).")
}

# Prefer personal library + optional local MSstats renv tree used in development
user_lib <- file.path(
  Sys.getenv("HOME"),
  "R",
  paste0(R.version$platform, "-library"),
  paste(R.version$major, strsplit(R.version$minor, ".", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]][[1L]], sep = ".")
)
ms_renv_lib <- file.path(
  Sys.getenv("HOME"),
  ".cache/R/renv/library/test_MSstats-b57ec874/linux-ubuntu-noble/R-4.6/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu"
)
extra_libs <- c(user_lib, ms_renv_lib)
extra_libs <- extra_libs[dir.exists(extra_libs)]
if (length(extra_libs) > 0L) {
  .libPaths(unique(c(extra_libs, .libPaths())))
}

needed <- c("MSstats", "MSstatsConvert", "data.table")
missing_pkgs <- needed[!vapply(needed, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing_pkgs) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "Install missing packages first: ",
    paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = ", "),
    "\nExample: BiocManager::install(c(\"MSstats\", \"MSstatsConvert\"))",
    "\nCurrent .libPaths():\n  ", paste(.libPaths(), collapse = "\n  ")
  )
}

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(MSstats)
  library(MSstatsConvert)
  library(data.table)
  library(dplyr)
})

if (requireNamespace("pkgload", quietly = TRUE)) {
  pkgload::load_all(pkg_dir, quiet = TRUE)
} else if (requireNamespace("devtools", quietly = TRUE)) {
  devtools::load_all(pkg_dir, quiet = TRUE)
} else {
  stop("Install pkgload or devtools to load the local OlinkAnalyze package.")
}
```

## Locate DIA-NN tinytest data

Prefer the copy installed with `MSstatsConvert`. If that is unavailable
(older CRAN builds may omit `tinytest/`), fall back to a local cache path
or download from the GitHub `devel` tree.

Source on GitHub:
[MSstatsConvert/tree/devel/inst/tinytest/raw_data/DIANN](https://github.com/Vitek-Lab/MSstatsConvert/tree/devel/inst/tinytest/raw_data/DIANN)

```{r}
#| label: locate-diann-data
diann_dir <- system.file(
  "tinytest", "raw_data", "DIANN",
  package = "MSstatsConvert"
)

if (!nzchar(diann_dir) || !dir.exists(diann_dir)) {
  # Optional local fallback used during development
  fallback <- path.expand(
    "~/.cache/R/renv/library/test_MSstats-b57ec874/linux-ubuntu-noble/R-4.6/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/MSstatsConvert/tinytest/raw_data/DIANN"
  )
  if (dir.exists(fallback)) {
    diann_dir <- fallback
    message("Using local fallback DIANN tinytest directory.")
  } else {
    stop(
      "Could not find MSstatsConvert DIANN tinytest data.\n",
      "Install a build that includes inst/tinytest/, or clone:\n",
      "  https://github.com/Vitek-Lab/MSstatsConvert/tree/devel"
    )
  }
}

diann_report_path <- file.path(diann_dir, "diann_input.tsv")
annotation_path <- file.path(diann_dir, "annotation.csv")

stopifnot(file.exists(diann_report_path), file.exists(annotation_path))
list(
  diann_dir = diann_dir,
  report = basename(diann_report_path),
  annotation = basename(annotation_path)
)
```

### Peek at inputs

```{r}
#| label: peek-inputs
diann_report <- data.table::fread(diann_report_path)
annotation <- data.table::fread(annotation_path)

list(
  report_dim = dim(diann_report),
  report_cols = names(diann_report)[seq_len(min(8L, ncol(diann_report)))],
  annotation = annotation
)
```

The annotation maps each `Run` to a `Condition` and `BioReplicate` (here:
`0.1fmol` vs `0.25fmol`).

## Convert DIA-NN → MSstats format

`DIANNtoMSstatsFormat()` produces the feature-level table MSstats expects
(ProteinName, peptide/feature columns, Intensity, Condition, …).

```{r}
#| label: diann-to-msstats
msstats_input <- DIANNtoMSstatsFormat(
  input = diann_report,
  annotation = annotation,
  MBR = FALSE,
  use_log_file = FALSE
)

dim(msstats_input)
utils::head(msstats_input, 3L)
```

## Summarise to protein level

`dataProcess()` aggregates features to protein-level log-intensities
(`ProteinLevelData`), which is the table `MSstatstoNPX()` expects.

```{r}
#| label: data-process
processed <- dataProcess(
  msstats_input,
  use_log_file = FALSE
)

protein_level <- processed$ProteinLevelData
dim(protein_level)
utils::head(protein_level, 3L)
```

Key columns for the next step:

| MSstats column | Role in NPX conversion |
|----------------|------------------------|
| `Protein` | → `UniProt` / `Assay` (+ synthetic `OlinkID`) |
| `LogIntensities` | → `NPX` |
| `originalRUN` | → `SampleID` |
| `GROUP` | → `Condition` / `PlateID` |
| `SUBJECT` | → `Subject` |
| `more50missing` | contributes to `QC_Warning` |

## Convert protein level → NPX with `MSstatstoNPX()`

```{r}
#| label: msstats-to-npx
npx <- MSstatstoNPX(
  data = protein_level,
  panel = "MSstats/DIANN protein",
  check = TRUE,
  clean = FALSE
)

dim(npx)
colnames(npx)
utils::head(npx, 5L)
```

```{r}
#| label: npx-summary
dplyr::count(npx, SampleID, Condition)
dplyr::count(npx, QC_Warning)
```

Optional: persist for downstream scripts.

```{r}
#| label: write-npx
out_dir <- "results"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
out_csv <- file.path(out_dir, "diann_msstats_protein_npx.csv")
utils::write.csv(npx, out_csv, row.names = FALSE)
out_csv
```

## Quick OlinkAnalyze look

Drop non-finite NPX before plotting / testing. With two conditions in the
tinytest annotation, a simple t-test is possible.

```{r}
#| label: olink-dist
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
npx_plot <- dplyr::filter(npx, is.finite(NPX))

if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  olink_dist_plot(npx_plot, color_g = "Condition")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: olink-ttest
npx_ttest <- npx_plot |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[["Condition"]])) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Condition = factor(.data[["Condition"]]))

n_cond <- nlevels(npx_ttest$Condition)
if (n_cond == 2L) {
  # Keep proteins measured in both conditions with >=2 samples each
  keep_oids <- npx_ttest |>
    dplyr::count(.data[["OlinkID"]], .data[["Condition"]]) |>
    dplyr::group_by(.data[["OlinkID"]]) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      n_cond = dplyr::n(),
      min_n = min(.data[["n"]]),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::filter(.data[["n_cond"]] == 2L, .data[["min_n"]] >= 2L) |>
    dplyr::pull(.data[["OlinkID"]])

  if (length(keep_oids) == 0L) {
    message(
      "Tinytest DIANN set is too sparse for olink_ttest() ",
      "(need >=2 samples per Condition for some proteins)."
    )
  } else {
    npx_ttest <- dplyr::filter(npx_ttest, .data[["OlinkID"]] %in% keep_oids)
    ttest_results <- tryCatch(
      olink_ttest(npx_ttest, variable = "Condition"),
      error = function(e) {
        message("olink_ttest() skipped: ", conditionMessage(e))
        NULL
      }
    )
    if (!is.null(ttest_results)) {
      utils::head(dplyr::arrange(ttest_results, .data[["Adjusted_pval"]]), 10L)
    }
  }
} else {
  message(
    "Need exactly 2 Condition levels for olink_ttest(); found ",
    n_cond, ": ",
    paste(levels(npx_ttest$Condition), collapse = ", ")
  )
}
```

## Summary

| Step | Function | Output |
|------|----------|--------|
| Read DIANN tinytest | `fread(diann_input.tsv)` + `annotation.csv` | DIA-NN report |
| Feature-level MSstats | `DIANNtoMSstatsFormat()` | 11-column MSstats table |
| Protein summarisation | `dataProcess()` | `ProteinLevelData` |
| NPX-style long table | `MSstatstoNPX()` | OlinkAnalyze-ready tibble |

Synthetic `OlinkID`s (`OID#####`) are assigned per protein so helpers that
expect an Olink ID column can run. They are **not** real Olink assay IDs.
